title: unique_ptr basics
concept: unique_ptr guarantees sole ownership and is automatically deleted when the scope ends.

steps.title: create unique_ptr
steps.explanation:
`make_unique<int>(42)` allocates an int on the heap and wraps it in a unique_ptr.

`unique_ptr` is a pointer to which RAII is applied. Since it has only one owner, it cannot be copied and is automatically `delete`ed upon destruction.

steps.title: Dereference for access
steps.explanation: Access the value like a regular pointer with `*p`. The method of use is the same as the raw pointer.

steps.title: Automatic cleanup
steps.explanation:
When `main` ends with `return 0;`, `p`'s destructor is called and the heap memory is automatically freed.

**No need to call delete directly** — this is the core value of smart pointers.

quiz.question: What is wrong with the description of unique_ptr?
options: Can be copied to another unique_ptr
It is recommended to create it with make_unique
quiz.explanation: unique_ptr cannot be copied because the copy constructor/assignment operator has been removed. To transfer ownership, you must use std::move.

misconceptions.wrong: unique_ptr can be assigned to another variable.
misconceptions.correct: Copying is prohibited, and ownership can only be transferred with std::move.
misconceptions.why: Deleting the same memory in two places causes a double-free bug, so limit the owner to one.

keyTakeaway: unique_ptr is the most basic smart pointer that fundamentally prevents memory leaks through RAII.
